model_fitness.best_available_model: Tsc1-GFAP conditional knockout mouse (Tsc1^flox/flox; GFAP-Cre), with continuous video-EEG seizure quantification; the same model in which astrocytic IL-1b/CXCL10 elevation (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087) and elevated brain VEGF with two-photon-confirmed BBB leak plus apatinib/RepSox intervention (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:38049961) were demonstrated.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Yes for the specific question asked. It reproduces Tsc1 loss, mTORC1 hyperactivation, spontaneous recurrent seizures, astrocytic IL-1b/CXCL10 induction and BBB leak, and it is rapamycin-responsive — so it can support a factorial rapamycin x anti-axis design (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087; PMID:38049961). It does not model the two-hit somatic architecture or human cortical tubers (INFERENCE, inconclusive).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Partially. Astrocytes are the driven cell type and are the putative IL-1b source (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087), and brain microvascular endothelium shows the VEGF/BBB phenotype (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:38049961). But GFAP-Cre deletion is astrocyte-biased, whereas human epileptogenesis involves dysmorphic neurons and giant cells arising from radial glia; the neuronal-lesional compartment is under-represented (INFERENCE, contradictory).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Spontaneous seizure frequency and total seizure burden by continuous video-EEG; survival; plus mechanistic readouts (cortical/hippocampal IL-1b and CXCL10, phospho-S6, BBB permeability by tracer extravasation or two-photon imaging) (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087; PMID:38049961).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Single-model dependence — the entire hypothesis rests on this one conditional knockout (INFERENCE, inconclusive, PMID:38049961). Rapamycin is near-curative for seizures in this model, which compresses the ceiling for detecting incremental add-on benefit and may force a submaximal-rapamycin reference arm. Apatinib is a P-gp substrate with limited CNS exposure and RepSox is a non-clinical tool compound, so mouse-level target engagement does not read through to a translatable molecule (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID:38049961). Astrocyte-restricted Cre over-weights the glial contribution.

plan.critical_question: Does blocking the VEGFR/BBB or IL-1 axis reduce seizure burden ON TOP of mTORC1 inhibition — i.e. is any part of this axis an mTOR-independent causal driver rather than a reversible downstream readout of mTORC1 hyperactivation?
plan.proposed_experiment: Factorial add-on study in Tsc1-GFAP CKO mice (n~12-15/arm, both sexes, randomised, blinded scoring), 6 arms: (1) vehicle; (2) submaximal rapamycin (a dose titrated to ~50% seizure-burden reduction, deliberately leaving headroom to detect addition); (3) submaximal rapamycin + apatinib (VEGFR2); (4) submaximal rapamycin + IL-1 axis blockade (IL-1R antagonism or a caspase-1 inhibitor as the CNS-oriented small-molecule option); (5) near-maximal rapamycin alone as the efficacy ceiling; (6) apatinib or IL-1 blockade as monotherapy (secondary, for interpretation only). Treat from P21 (post-symptom-onset) with continuous video-EEG from P25 to endpoint. Mandatory pharmacodynamic gate measured in the same animals: brain-tissue drug concentration and target engagement (cortical phospho-VEGFR2 for apatinib; cortical mature IL-1b for the IL-1 arm) — a negative efficacy result is uninterpretable without proof the target was engaged in brain.
plan.model: Tsc1^flox/flox;GFAP-Cre mouse with continuous video-EEG; the published model for both the inflammatory and neurovascular phenotypes (PMID:26003087; PMID:38049961).
plan.primary_readout: Total seizure burden (seconds of electrographic seizure per 24 h) over the recording window, compared between submaximal-rapamycin alone and submaximal-rapamycin + add-on. Secondary: seizure frequency, survival, cortical IL-1b/CXCL10, BBB tracer leak, phospho-S6.
plan.supportive_result: Add-on arm shows a clear, pre-specified incremental reduction in seizure burden over submaximal rapamycin alone (e.g. >=40% further reduction, p<0.05) WITH documented brain target engagement, and ideally residual benefit even against near-maximal rapamycin. This would establish an mTOR-independent causal contribution and justify moving to the agent problem — specifically a medicinal-chemistry effort for a CNS-penetrant, chronically paediatric-dosable IL-1 axis inhibitor, since neither apatinib nor RepSox is a viable clinical molecule.
plan.negative_result: No incremental seizure-burden reduction over submaximal rapamycin despite confirmed brain target engagement and confirmed suppression of the axis biomarker (IL-1b/CXCL10 or BBB leak). This is the expected outcome given that mTORC1 inhibition alone already reverses these markers (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:26003087), and it would mean the axis is an epiphenomenon.
plan.decision_enabled: Go/no-go on the entire neurovascular-neuroinflammatory programme in TSC, for a few hundred thousand dollars and ~6-9 months. Negative => stop; redirect resources to brain-penetrant/tissue-selective mTOR inhibition and to earlier/preventive dosing, which is where the unmet need actually sits. Positive => fund de novo CNS-penetrant chemistry on the IL-1 node and only then consider clinical translation; do NOT advance apatinib or any chronic systemic anti-angiogenic into a paediatric lifelong indication regardless of result (INFERENCE, contradictory — hypertension, growth-plate and wound-healing toxicity, on top of existing angiomyolipoma bleeding risk). HYPOTHESIS (not_studied): a partial-rapamycin-sparing combination could widen the therapeutic window; this experiment is the only cheap test of it.

model_fitness.best_available_model: Tsc1-GFAP CKO mouse with continuous video-EEG, dosed with high-dose systemic or intracerebroventricular IL-1Ra (anakinra) — but note the model's fitness here is limited less by the biology than by the fact that no biologic exists that reaches the relevant compartment in humans. For the VEGF arm, the same model with a systemic VEGF ligand trap is adequate because the target is luminal.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: For the IL-1 arm, yes at the biology level: astrocyte-localised IL-1b and CXCL10 are elevated in neocortex and hippocampus and are a defined extracellular ligand a biologic could neutralise (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087). For the VEGF arm, elevated brain VEGF with abnormal vessel anatomy and BBB leak is reproduced (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:38049961). Neither captures the human delivery constraint, which is the actual blocker.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Astrocytes (IL-1 source) and brain microvascular endothelium (VEGF-responsive) are both present and phenotypically abnormal (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID:26003087; PMID:38049961). However, the mouse BBB does not faithfully predict human biologic CNS exposure, so a positive ICV result in mouse would not de-risk the human route (INFERENCE, contradictory).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Seizure burden by continuous video-EEG, with CSF-to-plasma ratio of the biologic and cortical IL-1b/phospho-IL-1R signalling as the obligatory engagement readouts.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Decisive limitation is route, not model. Standard subcutaneous anakinra achieves only a small single-digit percentage of plasma concentration in CSF, so parenchymal astrocytic IL-1 signalling is unlikely to be engaged at tolerated systemic doses (INFERENCE, contradictory); FIRES practice pushes high-dose IV or intrathecal routes (EVIDENCE, supportive for tolerability only, PMID:33681649). No BBB-shuttle-engineered IL-1Ra or anti-IL-1b exists; TfR1 shuttle platforms are clinical-stage for enzymes but have never been applied to cytokine blockade, so this is a de novo engineering programme, not repurposing (INFERENCE, contradictory). An ICV mouse experiment can prove the biology but cannot create a human delivery path. A ClinicalTrials.gov search for TSC + anakinra returned 0 studies (EVIDENCE, contradictory).

plan.critical_question: Before any delivery engineering: is parenchymal IL-1 signalling a causal, mTOR-independent seizure driver in TSC at all? Framed as a biology-first question deliberately, because the delivery path for a parenchymally-acting IL-1 biologic does not currently exist, so spending on delivery before proving the biology is the wrong order.
plan.proposed_experiment: Ceiling-test by route-bypass, not by a clinical-route biologic. In Tsc1-GFAP CKO mice on submaximal rapamycin, deliver IL-1Ra directly into the CNS by chronic intracerebroventricular minipump (bypassing the BBB entirely to maximise the chance of a positive signal), versus submaximal rapamycin + vehicle ICV, versus near-maximal rapamycin alone (n~12-15/arm, randomised, blinded). Measure CSF IL-1Ra concentration and cortical IL-1b/downstream IL-1R signalling to prove engagement. Run the systemic VEGF ligand trap as a separate, parallel low-cost arm since that target is luminal and needs no BBB crossing. Treat this as a kill experiment: if saturating CNS IL-1Ra exposure adds nothing on top of rapamycin, no amount of shuttle engineering can rescue the programme.
plan.model: Tsc1^flox/flox;GFAP-Cre mouse, continuous video-EEG, chronic ICV infusion (biology-maximal route) plus a systemic anti-VEGF arm (PMID:26003087; PMID:38049961).
plan.primary_readout: Incremental reduction in total seizure burden over submaximal rapamycin alone, conditional on documented CSF exposure and cortical IL-1 pathway engagement.
plan.supportive_result: Saturating ICV IL-1Ra produces a substantial pre-specified incremental seizure-burden reduction on top of rapamycin with confirmed engagement. Even then the decision is NOT 'start a trial' — it is 'the biology justifies a de novo BBB-shuttle IL-1Ra engineering programme or an intrathecal-route feasibility study', an expensive multi-year commitment that should only be entered with this result in hand.
plan.negative_result: No incremental benefit despite saturating CNS exposure — consistent with IL-1b/CXCL10 being obligate downstream readouts already normalised by mTORC1 inhibition (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID:26003087). Kills the IL-1 biologic arm permanently.
plan.decision_enabled: Current recommendation, independent of this experiment: do not fund a protein/biologic programme in this axis now. The two arms' advantages do not combine — the IL-1 arm has the seizure-proximal, astrocyte-localised story but no parenchymal delivery path, while the VEGF arm has approved luminal-acting traps but an indirect route to seizure control and an unacceptable chronic anti-angiogenic risk profile in growing children with existing angiomyolipoma bleeding risk (INFERENCE, contradictory). Hence conclusion NO PLAUSIBLE DELIVERY PATH. The ICV experiment above is worth running only as a cheap rider on the small-molecule add-on study, to decide whether the IL-1 node ever deserves a delivery-engineering investment. HYPOTHESIS (not_studied): focal BBB leak in TSC lesions might improve local biologic access where it is most needed; this is unproven, would be spatially uneven, and should not be assumed as a delivery strategy.
